At normal operating conditions, the system will process 1,290 metric tonnes of CO per day, assuming 355 operating days per year and an ethanol production 2 rate of 160 million gallons per year. The proposed process trains a multistage centrifugal blower with a five-stage reciprocating compressor, delivering CO to the injection wellhead at up to 1,500 psig. Triethylene glycol (TEG) 2 dehydration, applied after the fourth compression stage, reduces water content to a target of 10 lb/MMscf, well within the 30 lb/MMscf injection limit. Beyond dehydration, no additional treatment is required; trace impurities including oxygen and nitrogen will remain in the injected stream. Key design considerations include the absence of spare cooling tower capacity at the site, necessitating new cooling infrastructure, and the need for a new electrical substation to support large motor loads. The facility is designed for continuous, largely unattended operation, monitored around the clock by existing OEE operations staff. This document serves as the foundational reference for all subsequent detailed engineering activities associated with the OEE CO injection facility. 2 iii Table of Contents DISCLAIMER This also equates to 1,290 tonnes/day of CO 2 based on 355 operating days/year. It is based on an ethanol production rate of 160 MM gallons/year. The CO 2 will be injected into a local saline aquifer formation, located approximately 4 miles from the ethanol plant. Sampling data from the CO 2 stream leaving the ethanol plant (August 2019) show that the oxygen (O ) concentration ranges from 14 2 ppmv to 1,300 ppmv. The plant will be designed to meet injection-grade CO 2 specifications without the removal of oxygen from the source CO . For this reason, the basis for the OEE facility is to use 2 compression to boost the pressure to injection conditions and triethylene glycol (TEG) dehydration to remove water from the CO 2 prior to injection.
